newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Gencor reiterates interest in Venezuela CVG sale.
newsitem.headline: Gencor reiterates interest in Venezuela CVG sale.

text.p: South African mining company Gencor Billington International reiterated Friday its interest in Venezuela's upcoming aluminum privatization, but said much remained to be done before the sale could go ahead.

The sale "is important for the world's aluminum market ... but there are a number of details that remain to be sorted out," Gencor president Brian Gilberston told reporters after sitting in on the weekly meeting of the economic cabinet.

Venezuela expects to sell by the end of the year state- holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana's (CVG) four aluminum companies -- smelters Venalum and Alcasa, bauxite producer Bauxilum and carbon anode manufacturer Carbonorca.

Blessed with cheap supplies of electricity and ready supplies of ore, the complex produces over 600,000 tonnes of aluminum per year. However, Gilberston said issues such as the treatment of environmental liabilities, the terms of the bauxite concession, electricity contracts and taxes at the municipal level still had to be dealt with.
Gencor is one of 13 companies pre-selected to bid in the auction. Others including Alcoa, Alumax, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro ASA and RTZ Corp.
